title: Help, reporting protections and the Workplace Justice visa
topic: migrant worker protections and workplace exploitation
content: The page says temporary visa holders, permanent residents and Australian citizens can seek help about workplace exploitation and workplace rights.
The page identifies exploitation concerns including pay and wages, leave and entitlements, discrimination, passport retention, visa threats, excessive work hours, unsafe housing and underpayment.
The page says employers cannot cancel a worker's visa; visa decisions are made by the Australian Government.
The page describes reporting protections for eligible temporary visa holders who experienced workplace exploitation connected to a work-related visa condition breach.
The page says the Fair Work Ombudsman or an Accredited Third Party may certify a workplace exploitation matter for reporting protections, subject to the applicable process and circumstances.
The page lists preparation information for a protection request, including certification of workplace exploitation, visa information and details of a work-related visa breach when applicable.
